summary: The study describes two new ALD processes for depositing PbS thin films at low temperatures (45−155 °C) using volatile and reactive lead precursors Pb(dbda) and Pb(btsa)2 along with H2S. These processes enable direct ALD of PbS onto halide perovskites like CH3NH3PbI3 (MAPI) without decomposition, improving the stability of the perovskite. The films exhibit p-type conductivity with good mobility (10−70 cm2 V−1 s−1) and are uniform, crystalline, and pure. The study highlights the compatibility of these ALD processes with perovskites and their potential for use in optoelectronic devices.
evidence: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) is a viable method for depositing functional, passivating, and encapsulating layers on top of halide perovskites. We describe two new ALD processes for lead sulﬁde. These processes operate at low deposition temperatures (45−155 °C) that have been inaccessible to previous ALD PbS processes. Our processes rely on volatile and reactive lead precursors Pb(dbda) and Pb(btsa)2 as well as H2S. These precursors produce high quality PbS thin films that are uniform, crystalline, and pure. The films exhibit p-type conductivity and good mobilities of 10−70 cm2 V−1 s−1. Low deposition temperatures enable direct ALD of PbS onto a halide perovskite CH3NH3PbI3 (MAPI) without its decomposition.
